title: Convert Cp to Cv
action: Compute constant‑volume heat capacity Cv from the provided smoothed Cp data using the thermal expansion correction. Apply the Grüneisen relation with γ=1.43 (or equivalently the Nernst‑Lindemann approximation with a = 5.41×10⁻⁷ J⁻¹·mol) as described in the methodology. The correction may use the exact expression (β²V/κ)T below 550 K and the Grüneisen approximation above.
description: Prepare the Cv dataset required for the subsequent anharmonic fit. The procedure uses literature expansion parameters (β, V, κ at 550 K) to derive γ and a, then corrects Cp→Cv for all temperatures.

title: Fit anharmonic terms and produce heat capacity table
action: Using the computed Cv values, perform a linear least‑squares fit of (Cv - 9R)/T against T⁻³ for temperatures T ≥ 650 K to obtain the anharmonic coefficient A (intercept) and high‑temperature Debye temperature θ∞ (from slope). Compute the Einstein temperature θE from θ∞ and the literature Debye temperature θD = 778 K via θ∞² = (1/6)θD² + (25/18)θE². Compute the harmonic heat capacity Ch = 0.5[3R·D(θD/T) + 15R·E(θE/T)] for all temperatures in the Cp dataset. Calculate the anharmonic contribution Ca = Cv - Ch. Write the full table to the specified CSV file.
description: Complete temperature‑dependent heat capacity table containing Cv, the harmonic model Ch, and the anharmonic difference. The hidden checker recomputes A and θE from the Cv column for T≥650 K, deriving the scored quantities without trusting the agent’s reported parameters.
output_schema: CSV with header: T (K), Cp (J/mol/K), Cv (J/mol/K), Ch (J/mol/K), anharmonic (J/mol/K). Rows correspond to all temperatures from the input Cp dataset.

title: Record fitted parameters
action: Write the fitted anharmonic coefficient A, Einstein temperature θE, and high‑temperature Debye temperature θ∞ as a JSON object to the specified file.
description: Machine‑readable record of the key derived parameters. The checker cross‑checks these values against those recomputed from the CSV for structural consistency.
output_schema: JSON object with keys: "anharmonic_coefficient_A" (number, J/mol/K²), "einstein_temperature_thetaE" (number, K), "high_temp_debye_theta_inf" (number, K).
